question: Who was the main proponent of the Young Bengal Movement whose followers cherished the ideals of the French Revolution (1789 AD) and the liberal thinking of Britain?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Henry Louis Vivian Derozio**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Henry Louis Vivian Derozio was the main proponent of the Young Bengal Movement.
 
• He was a teacher and poet of Portuguese-Indian descent.
 
• Derozio's followers, known as Derozians, cherished the ideals of the French Revolution and liberal thinking of Britain.
 
• He taught at Hindu College, Calcutta, where he inspired his students to embrace free thinking and rationalism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Young Bengal Movement**

 
 
• It was a movement in 19th-century Bengal spearheaded by **Henry Louis Vivian Derozio.**
 
• The movement promoted rational thinking, freedom of thought, and social reform.
 
• The Derozians questioned traditional practices and campaigned for women's rights and education.
 
• It played a significant role in the Bengal Renaissance, which was a period of cultural, social, and intellectual awakening in Bengal.
 
 
 
• **French Revolution (1789 AD)**
 
 
• The **French Revolution** was a period of radical social and political change in France.
 
• It led to the overthrow of the monarchy, the establishment of a republic, and significant societal reforms.
 
• The Revolution's ideals of liberty, equality, and fraternity had a profound influence worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Liberal Thinking of Britain**
 
 
• Liberalism in Britain during the 19th century emphasized individual rights, civil liberties, and democracy.
 
• Key figures included John Stuart Mill, who advocated for freedom of expression and utilitarianism.
 
• The liberal ideas influenced many social reforms, such as the abolition of slavery and the expansion of suffrage.
